question: How do you handle eBilling and A/R?
html:
Frontline already supports eBilling and accounts receivable (A/R) for law firms. Over the next two and a half years we plan to consolidate that work into one billing service, with AI agents priced on how fast clients get paid (Frontline growth plan).

Why billing needs attention now

  • Client-side AI is rejecting more law-firm invoices. Rejections have risen from 11% to 18% (Frontline growth plan).
  • Each rejected invoice adds rework and pushes cash further out. Firms feel this in their A/R, not just in billing operations.

How the service is evolving

ElementWhat it means for a firmTiming
Consolidated eBilling and A/ROne provider for invoice submission, rejection handling and collections follow-upMonths 12 to 30 of the growth plan
Four finance agentsAI agents working the billing and A/R cycleSame phase
Pricing on days-to-payFees tied to how quickly invoices are paid, not to hours workedSame phase
Specialist billing capacityAdds experienced legal-billing teams through targeted acquisitionsSame phase

All timing comes from the growth plan (Frontline growth plan). It is a plan, not a delivered result.

What we cannot yet confirm

  • Service scope: The source material does not list today's eBilling scope, staffing or service levels. A current service catalogue would answer that.
  • Client results: No Frontline client rejection rates or days-to-pay baselines are available. Client-level A/R ageing and rejection logs would let us quote real before-and-after figures.
  • Agent pricing: The four agents and their pricing are planned, not yet published.

Where this fits for mid-size firms

  • The growth plan targets 143 mid-size firms (17,042 attorneys) in a 16-metro screen. Of these, 37 score 65 or above for fit (Mid-size law firms).
  • Many of the top-ranked firms are recommended a bundled offer (Mid-size law firms). Billing and A/R could become part of that bundle (est.).

Billing is where the plan turns into cash. The KPI roadmap assumes about $25M of acquired revenue by month 24 and about $55M by month 36, partly from revenue-cycle add-ons (est., Frontline growth plan). Frontline was bought at roughly 12 to 15 times EBITDA (est., Frontline public filings), so earnings growth has to carry the return. A days-to-pay product that measurably cuts rejections is one of the clearest ways to earn more per firm.

Next actions

  • Publish a current eBilling and A/R service description so this answer can describe live scope, not just the plan.
  • Pull rejection rates and days-to-pay baselines for a sample of existing clients. Pricing on days-to-pay needs these benchmarks before launch.
  • Define the four finance agents and their pricing so customer-facing copy can name them.
  • Agree with deal and legal teams which parts of the billing acquisition plan can be discussed publicly.
